description: Prepare a three-node group under node 1; move node 1 into the runtime actor. Isolate its generated acceptance of notify value 42. Nodes 2 and 3 acquire a newer ballot and decide 99 at slot 1. Restore node 1 through actual preparation and synchronization before its first five-second tick, then observe its pending result and decided content.

harness.description: Mixed public-API actor/core driver with conforming Tokio AsyncRuntime adapter. Real five-second timer permits construction before notifier polling.
semantic_changes: No target modifications. Custom AsyncRuntime uses tokio::spawn and tokio::time::sleep without altered time.
Other two replicas are driven synchronously through core APIs. An unused node-1 placeholder preserves vector indexing and never receives protocol traffic.

legality.derivation: Initial public prepare completes before actor ownership transfer. Admission is witnessed by two generated AcceptDecide messages for 42; neither reaches peers. The new quorum excludes the old leader, then a restored PrepareReq/Prepare/Promise/AcceptSync exchange replaces its log with actual decided 99. Incoming queue dispatch precedes following read commands because run prioritizes incoming over commands; read returns actual decided state. Setup asserts completion before the first five-second timer, but does not require any principal result. Timeout bounds missing completion rather than claiming a deadline violation. Event channel capacity exceeds generated state changes and needs no independent consumer for this finite run.
legality.applicability: One actor owning a locally assigned notify call; two other core replicas; non-Byzantine three-node configuration, no snapshots, default MemoryStorage, public API transport and a real Tokio timer.
alternatives: A changed ballot alone does not prove value loss: a new leader may adopt the entry. This check instead establishes an actual different decided value at the returned position.

grounding.derivation: One operation identity is declared before the result. The observed replacement prerequisite independently establishes a different decided entry before the notifier tick. For an actual successful result, read_decided_suffix returns the content at returned index minus one, following the runtime index convention demonstrated by the existing test.

observable_properties.description: If the notify call succeeds, its returned index must contain its submitted value; observed non-success is bounded holds and does not prove universal notifier correctness.
